claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

  - Child is not in hospital or residential accommodation

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start by accessing the eligibility assessment tool.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To start your eligibility assessment, I need to know about your child(ren).

**Could you tell me:**

1. **How many children are you enquiring about?** (Or are you enquiring about one specific child?)
2. **How old is/are your child(ren)?**

Child Benefit eligibility depends on the child's age, so this is the first thing we need to check:

- **Under 16**: Children are usually eligible
- **16-19**: Eligibility depends on whether they're in approved education or training
- **20 and over**: Generally not eligible for Child Benefit

Please provide the names and ages of the child(ren) you're asking about, and we'll work through the eligibility requirements together.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I'm asking about my son Alex. He's 18 years old and still living at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information! So you're asking about your son **Alex who is 18 years old**.

Since Alex is 18, he falls into the **16-19 age category**. For this age group, Child Benefit eligibility depends on whether he's in approved education or training.

**Can you tell me: Is Alex currently in any of the following?**

- Full-time education (e.g., school, college, university)
- An apprenticeship
- Approved vocational training
- Or is he not in any of these?

This will help me determine if he qualifies for Child Benefit.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex is still in college doing his A-levels. He's studying full-time.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Thank you for that information. Since Alex is 18 and in full-time education (A-levels at college), this is a key factor for his eligibility.

Let me navigate through the assessment based on this information.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! Now I need to confirm: Alex is currently **in education** (full-time A-levels). Let me check the specific requirements for his education level.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! I can see that Alex is doing **A-levels**, which is on the approved list of qualifications for 16-19 year olds. 

Now I need to check a few more details to ensure he meets all the criteria:

**A few quick questions about Alex:**

1. **Is he studying full-time** (at least 12 hours per week of supervised study)? You mentioned he's full-time, so I assume yes?

2. **Is he employed/working?** Specifically, is he working full-time or part-time alongside his studies?

3. **Is Alex married?** (This is relevant for the 16-19 age group)

Once I have these details, I can give you the final eligibility outcome.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
Yes, he's studying full-time at college - definitely more than 12 hours a week of classes and coursework. 

No, he's not working at all - he's just focused on his studies.

And no, he's not married.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Thank you for confirming those details. Alex meets all the key criteria so far:

✓ He's 18 years old
✓ He's in full-time education (A-levels)
✓ A-levels are approved education
✓ He's studying more than 12 hours per week
✓ He's not working full-time
✓ He's not married

Let me navigate through the final checks to confirm his eligibility.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Since Alex isn't working at all, he definitely meets this criterion. Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check: **Is Alex receiving any benefits in his own right, such as:**
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA)
- Universal Credit (as a claimant in his own right)

Or is he not receiving any of these benefits?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not receiving any benefits in his own right. He's just a student living at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! Alex doesn't receive any of those benefits. Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Good news - this check is about apprenticeships. Since Alex is doing A-levels at college (not an apprenticeship), he clearly passes this criterion. Let me move forward.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check your residency status, as this is an important requirement for Child Benefit eligibility.

**Can you tell me:**

1. **Do you normally live in the UK?** (This is the most common path)

Or if you don't normally live in the UK, do you have any of the following:
- Settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme
- Pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme (and if so, what circumstances apply - working, studying, sufficient resources, etc.)
- Are you a Crown servant living abroad in a qualifying country

For most people, the answer is simply that they normally live in the UK, so just let me know your situation.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I normally live in the UK. I live here with Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! You meet the residency requirement. Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Now I need to confirm that you're responsible for Alex. The good news is you've already mentioned he's living at home with you, so this should be straightforward.

**To confirm - which of these applies to you:**

1. **You live with Alex** (which you've already mentioned)

OR

2. You contribute to Alex's upkeep (pay for his food, clothes, housing, etc.) even if he doesn't live with you full-time

Since you said Alex lives at home with you, the first option applies. Let me proceed.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check one more important thing:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?** 

For example:
- Is Alex's other parent (if applicable) also claiming Child Benefit for him?
- Or is anyone else claiming?

Or is it just you making the claim for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex. It's just me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Let me continue to the final checks.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check Alex's current living situation:

**Where is Alex living?**
- Is he living at home with you (normal living situation)
- Is he in hospital
- Is he in care
- Is he in a fostering arrangement

Since you mentioned he's living at home with you, I assume it's normal living, but let me confirm.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he's just living at home with me - normal living situation. Nothing special like hospital or care or anything like that.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Let me proceed with the final check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! We're almost at the end. Just one final question:

**Is the local council paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

In other words, is the council helping to pay for his housing or other living costs? Or are you fully supporting him?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, the council isn't paying anything towards Alex. I'm supporting him myself.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's all the information I need. Based on all the checks we've gone through, I can now provide you with your eligibility outcome.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent news! Now let me record your eligibility outcome:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## 🎉 **You Are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit!**

### Summary for Alex:
**Result:** ✅ **ELIGIBLE**

You can claim Child Benefit for your son Alex. He meets all the eligibility requirements as an 18-year-old in full-time approved education (A-levels).

### Key factors supporting his eligibility:
- ✅ Age 18 (within the eligible range for education)
- ✅ In full-time approved education (A-levels)
- ✅ Studying more than 12 hours per week
- ✅ Not working full-time
- ✅ Not receiving qualifying benefits
- ✅ You live in the UK and meet residency requirements
- ✅ You live with Alex and are responsible for him
- ✅ No one else is claiming for him
- ✅ Living normally at home
- ✅ Council is not funding his support

### Next Steps - How to Claim:

1. **Apply online or by post** using form CH2
2. **Provide proof of identity** for yourself and Alex
3. **Provide Alex's birth certificate or adoption certificate**
4. **Be aware of the High Income Child Benefit Charge** - if you or your partner earns over £60,000 per year, you may need to pay some or all of the benefit back through self-assessment
5. **Payment frequency** - Payments are usually made every 4 weeks

### Useful Links:
- [How to claim Child Benefit](https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim)
- [Child Benefit rates and payment dates](https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit)

**Congratulations, and best of luck with your claim!**
